articles.title: How a heated argument turned fatal for Kolkata techie; partner, her mom arrested
articles.description: A late-night argument inside a rented flat in Kolkata resulted in the death of a 25-year-old software engineer. The police have arrested the victim's live-in partner and her mother in connection with the incident. Witnesses reported hearing loud arguments before the attack occurred. The victim was discovered lying in a pool of blood after a woman sought help from neighbors.

articles.title: Wisconsin family manages 500-acre forest for wildlife and timber; shortlisted for state conservation award
articles.description: Jesse and Kylie Sebero are managing over 500 acres of forest in Marinette County, Wisconsin. They focus on timber production while ensuring ecological balance and wildlife conservation. The couple also opens their land for educational tours, helping others learn about forest management. They have been nominated for the 2026 Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award for their significant contributions. The award will be announced during an upcoming meeting on November 12.

articles.title: South Carolina woman protects 146-acre family land after promise to mother
articles.description: Alice Smith has placed her family's 146-acre property in South Carolina under a conservation easement, fulfilling a promise to her mother. articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex plunges over 400 points, Nifty50 slips below 25,000 levels
articles.full_text: Stock market today: Will Nifty50 touch 28,000 in 2027? BSE Sensex was trading 408.26 points, or 0.50%, lower at 80,591.14. However, some stocks bucked the weak market trend. SBI led the gainers, rising 1.86%, followed by NTPC, which gained 0.84%. ICICI Bank advanced 0.62%, while HDFC Bank was up 0.40%. IndiGo, Larsen & Toubro, Sun Pharma and Trent also traded in positive territory, gaining 0.36%, 0.29%, 0.26% and 0.22%, respectively. The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty opened lower on Monday, giving up some ground after ending the special Diwali Muhurat trading session in the red on Sunday. BSE Sensex was down 256.65 points, or 0.32%, at 80,742.75, while NSE Nifty slipped 41.80 points, or 0.17%, to 24,944.30. The benchmark indices had ended marginally lower during Sunday's special trading session to mark the beginning of Samvat 2083. After opening on a positive note, both indices failed to hold on to their gains amid profit-booking following a seven-day rally. The Sensex settled 28.62 points, or 0.04%, lower at 80,999.40, while the Nifty declined 43.95 points, or 0.18%, to close at 24,986.40. After a sharp weekly advance and a subdued Muhurat trading session, the market enters the new week facing a key test of momentum, with investors likely to weigh the scope for further gains against the prospect of near-term profit-taking. The immediate focus will be on whether underlying buying interest can sustain the recent advance, particularly against the backdrop of lingering global concerns surrounding the AI trade and ahead of Thursday's CPI data, which could provide the next significant directional cue for domestic equities. Stock market today: Rupee begins week strong, rises below 94 against US dollar Asian equity markets began the week on a relatively positive note, attempting to recover after a sharp technology-led selloff in the previous week. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan advanced 0.8%, following a 4.6% decline over the previous week. Japan's Nikkei rose 2.5%, while South Korean equities recorded smaller gains. Taiwan's benchmark also climbed around 2.5%, recovering after suffering its steepest weekly decline in two decades. The earlier selloff had been driven by concerns over the profitability of artificial intelligence investments and demand for the infrastructure supporting the technology. The developments had weighed particularly heavily on technology-heavy Asian markets. US stock futures were also slightly higher, following a recovery on Wall Street during Friday's session. Stock market today: Top stocks to buy on November 9 Indian benchmark indices were poised for a higher opening, with GIFT Nifty futures indicating a positive start for the domestic market. GIFT Nifty was trading at 25,057.5, compared with the Nifty 50's previous close of 24,986.40. The indication came after the Sensex and Nifty ended marginally lower during the special Muhurat trading session, consolidating after a seven-session winning streak. The possibility of a positive opening was supported by a decline in crude oil prices and optimism surrounding foreign investor inflows. However, potential profit-booking following the recent rally could limit the upside. The benchmark indices had advanced around 10.5% over the seven sessions through Friday, supported by foreign inflows, easing oil prices and the unwinding of global artificial intelligence-related trades. Oil prices declined at the start of the trading week after US President Donald Trump indicated that fresh American attacks on Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations to end the conflict continued to make progress. Brent crude futures fell 84 cents, or 0.85%, to $97.48 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude declined 32 cents, or 0.35%, to $90.51 per barrel. The decline reversed modest gains recorded during Friday's settlement, when markets were assessing the possibility of further US military action against Iran. Trump told CNN that renewed attacks were unlikely to be necessary if the two sides reached a strong agreement. However, both countries had reported attacks on ships in or near the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran had warned that it would retaliate against US and Israeli targets. Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty ended marginally lower during the special Muhurat trading session, snapping an eight-year streak of gains recorded during Diwali sessions since 2018. The indices began the session on a positive note but failed to sustain their early momentum as investors booked profits following a seven-session rally. The 30-share BSE Sensex declined 28.62 points, or 0.04%, to settle at 80,999.40, with 16 constituents ending higher and 14 lower. The index had touched an intraday high of 81,442.11, gaining 414.09 points, or 0.51%. The NSE Nifty also reversed its early gains, falling 43.95 points, or 0.18%, to close at 24,986.40.

articles.title: Maharashtra AYUSH Admission 2026: Special CAP Round 4 schedule announced for BAMS, BHMS and BUMS
articles.description: The Maharashtra State CET Cell has announced Special CAP Round 4 for BAMS, BHMS and BUMS admissions for 2026-27. Candidates must submit their online preferences by November 9, 2026, at 11.59 pm. The allotment list will be released on November 11. The special round follows approval for the newly established Government Ayurvedic College in Buldhana. After three CAP rounds, Maharashtra recorded 11,592 admissions across 13,750 seats, leaving 2,158 vacancies.

articles.title: MPSC Group C Recruitment 2026: Vacancies increased to 16,717, application window reopens on November 13
articles.description: MPSC Group C Recruitment 2026: The Maharashtra Public Service Commission has increased Group C recruitment vacancies from 5,707 to 16,717, adding 11,010 posts across government departments. The online application window will reopen from November 13 to November 27, 2026. The preliminary examination has been rescheduled to January 24, 2027, and eligible candidates will receive a one-year upper age limit relaxation. The examination will remain offline in OMR format, while 21 additional cadres have been incorporated into the recruitment plan.

articles.title: The ‘king’ who helped bring Rome to Britain in AD 43 may have been a woman; archaeologist challenges a 2,000-year-old assumption
articles.description: Archaeologist Miles Russell has proposed that Verica, the Iron Age ruler whose appeal to Roman Emperor Claudius may have helped trigger Rome's invasion of Britain in AD 43, could have been a woman. His theory draws on the ruler's name, coin imagery and inscriptions, alongside evidence of women's social status in Iron Age Britain. Although the claim remains unproven, it challenges traditional assumptions about political leadership and raises questions about Britain's pre-Roman history.

articles.title: Krishnasamy warns Kamal Haasan against using the 'Sandiyar' title
articles.description: Kamal Haasan's new film 'Sandiyar' is stirring controversy over possible caste-related violence. Krishnasamy, president of the New Tamilagam Party, has raised serious objections to the title, threatening legal action if it remains unchanged. This controversy mirrors a 2003 incident where Haasan altered a film's title due to protests. The ongoing debate highlights the sensitivity of caste issues within Tamil Nadu's society.
